Resumption must be refused when the halt left a partial or uncommitted event, when the log or state was externally tampered with, or when no new budget is available.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A partial event was written to durable storage before exhaustion (torn write).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The event log was externally mutated, truncated, or reordered during the pause.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The internal state at halt cannot be fully reconstructed from the committed log tail (hidden mutable state not captured by events).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The resuming process uses a different model version or configuration that changes deterministic behavior, breaking causal continuity.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"No new token budget is provisioned, causing immediate re-halt and potential incomplete writes.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Concurrent processes appended to the same log during the pause, creating identity collisions or gaps.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Append-only identity is preserved by monotonic sequence numbers or content hashes that make every committed event immutable. A clean halt guarantees the log tail is a well-formed boundary. On resumption, the process reads the tail, reconstructs state, and appends new events with strictly increasing identities. No prior identity is overwritten, reordered, or duplicated, so causal continuity is maintained.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
